newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Frankfurt, Vienna hit peaks, London well down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Frankfurt, Vienna hit peaks, London well down.

text.p: German and Austrian shares closed trade on Tuesday at record highs, boosted by the stronger dollar, but British stocks extended losses on inflation worries.
The dollar held steady against the mark but fell to its session low versus the yen as the yen rose to a 23-month high against the mark.
In metals, gold bounced off 12-year lows. New York gold futures opened higher on light fund buying after six consecutive days of declines.
But traders said spot gold remained vulnerable to testing $314 per ounce and possibly, falling below $300 within a few months.
Precious metals "have been going sideways for so long that now a trend has started. It will be very significant," said Fran Skelley, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.

The dollar's strength versus the mark lifted shares of German exporters, which led the DAX index to a sixth consecutive record high close. The DAX ended bourse trade up 33.56 points, or 0.8 percent, at 4,006.40.
Siemens AG hit a year high in Frankfurt after Britain's General Electric Co Plc said it was reviewing its GPT telecoms venture with Siemens.
Siemens was up 0.10 mark at 108.75, off its year high of 110.10 set early in the day.
Retailer Metro AG extended Monday's rally after Metro said it was talking with Dutch retailer SHV Holdings NV about taking over its cash and carry business.
Metro shares were up 10.90 marks at 216.40, off its year high of 219.00 set earlier in the day.
Austrian shares also climbed to its seventh consecutive record high close on the ATX index.
Oil and chemicals group OMV AG led the advance, surging 53 schillings to a year high of 1,677 before profit-taking emerged. OMV closed at 1,673, up 3.27 percent.

"The (ATX index's) basic tendency is positive, but the steep advance is over for the time being," a trader said. Most traders expected the ATX index to consolidate between 1,370 and 1,400 points in the near-term.
But those gains, the dollar's support for most European export shares and the Dow Jones Industrial Average's higher opening failed to pull other European bourses higher.
France's CAC-40 index slid amid profit-taking after its recent rally.

Alcatel Alsthom was among the biggest losers in Paris, shedding 1.77 percent to 777 French francs by 1425 GMT. Alcatel shares fell after General Electric Co Plc said it was in talks with Alcatel about the future of their GEC Alsthom joint venture.
Alcatel had no comment on the news.
London's FTSE-100 index extended losses on interest rate and currency worries.
British government debt prices fell, pushing long-term interest rates higher, after Britain's June retail price index (RPI) rose 0.4 percent to exceed forecasts for a 0.2-percent increase.
The RPI jump reinforced ideas the Bank of England would raise official rates at least 25 basis points at the end of its two-day policy meeting on Thursday.

"The market is anxious about rates," a dealer said. "If (Bank of England) doesn't move, the market will go down. If rates are raised by a quarter (point), it will not be enough. And if they go by half a point, it (will) be perceived as a lack of confidence in (finance minister Gordon) Brown."

If rates rise, traders worried sterling would climb further and chip away more profits from British companies with substantial overseas exposure. A strong currency makes a firm's goods and services more expensive abroad.
Sterling hit the highest level against the mark since May 1991 after the retail price report. Since then, it has fallen back nearly a pfennig.
A leading business survey said British engineering firms' second-quarter export orders fell to the lowest in three years because of the pound's surge.
Against the dollar, the pound slid back below 1.69.

In New York, the Dow was up 25.78 points at 7,884.27 at 1425 GMT. The Dow was boosted by bargain-hunting after Monday's downturn and active technology stocks before earning results due after New York's close.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 112.57 yen and 1.7560 marks compared to 112.30 and 1.7458 in late Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 50.6 points, or 1.05 percent, at 4,760.10.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed bourse trading up 33.56 points at 4,006.40.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 19.80 points at 2,927.86.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed firmer in London's afternoon at $320.80 per ounce, from $318.55 at London's close on Monday. Silver was at $4.34, up from $4.25 in early London but down from $4.45 at Monday's close in London.
